title: The Lethal Trifecta Is Already on Your Laptops — Michael Patterson, Coder
talk_summary: A Coder solutions engineer explains the 'lethal trifecta' of agent security (private data access + internet egress + untrusted content ingestion) and argues agents should run in isolated remote environments behind a model proxy and a process-level command firewall. It is mostly a security-architecture pitch for Coder's CDE product, but the three-layer pattern (remote sandbox, egress-restricted proxy, allowlisted command firewall) is directly copyable.

takeaways.technique: Remote isolated execution environment per agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents run in a pre-configured cloud VM/CDE rather than on a laptop or shared host, so they can only touch code, credentials, and data deliberately placed in that environment, and destructive commands cannot hit the host.

takeaways.technique: Model proxy as mandatory egress chokepoint
takeaways.what_they_do: All agent-to-LLM traffic goes through a proxy that logs every call, can strip secrets/PII from prompts, and can block unexpected destinations before reaching the provider.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before the agent hits the model provider, it goes to your proxy server, it goes through your gateway... it can sanitize, it can strip injections

takeaways.what_they_do: An agent firewall watches process execution and denies commands that were not pre-approved, e.g. destructive git or DB operations, regardless of what the prompt asked for.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if that agent for whatever reasons runs gh repo delete or drop this table, you want some kind of agentic firewall that's looking at the process logs and saying, 'Do not run this.'

takeaways.technique: Treat ingested content (CI logs, tickets, error messages) as untrusted
takeaways.what_they_do: Names prompt injection and context poisoning via error messages, support tickets, and CI/CD logs as the primary vector, since agents accept that text as ground truth.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it might be looking at error messages, it might be looking at support tickets, it might be looking at CICD logs... the agent just accepts that as a source of truth

takeaways.what_they_do: Give agents an environment already configured to run the project so they don't improvise dependency downloads from possibly contaminated registries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you put an agent on a fresh box and say, 'Download this GitHub repo and run the project.'... You never know where it's going to download things from

takeaways.technique: Alerting without alert fatigue on agent activity
takeaways.what_they_do: Warns that blanket alerting on all agent/LLM activity produces fatigue and masks real incidents; recommends targeted alerts on perimeter breaches only.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Once you get alert fatigue, you stop really looking at what's actually happening. Everything AI is doing just becomes noise
